description: What one index run did, in the same numbers `fathom index --stats` prints as a table. Owner: `e1.4`, surfaced by `e1.10`.

intent.description: What the intent capture (`e4.2`) recorded for this run, and what stream it came from. Every bucket is printed, including the empty one and the 'nothing recorded' one: missing intent is a state, and a state that only appears when it is non-empty is a state a reviewer never learns to read.

recorded.description: Episodes whose intent arrived as text - a prompt, an intent line, a task, a plan item.

from_hook.description: Of those, how many came from the harness stream rather than from a commit trailer.

digest_only.description: Episodes whose only intent evidence is a prompt digest: a request happened, its text was not sent.

none.description: Episodes with nothing recorded anywhere - the ticket's normal state, counted rather than hidden.

harness.description: The event stream the capture read. `events_file` is printed even when it does not exist, so 'no intent' can be told apart from 'no hooks' without a second command.

events_file.description: Where the stream was looked for, redacted to a repository-relative path.

exists.description: Whether a stream file was there at all.

turns.description: Turns the ledger holds, trimmed ones excluded.

events.description: Events the reader accepted on this pass.

refused.description: Lines the reader refused. Kept beside `turns` because an empty file and an unreadable file produce the same zero, and only one of them is normal.

notices.description: One line per thing the reader found and could not use, including a stream that exists but would not parse: 'no stream' and 'unreadable stream' are different reasons for the same empty intent tally, and only one of them is the repository's fault.

unreadable.description: Every commit this store cannot read out of the object database, named by id and by what the read said. A damaged or filter-cloned repository; the remedy is `git fsck`, never a fathom repair.

commit.description: The commit fathom tried to index.

seen_utc.description: When the index last tried this commit.

nothing_new.description: True when the run compared the refs with the store's last snapshot, found they said the same thing, and skipped the history walk, the analysis pass and the episode rebuild instead of repeating them (`reco-7tc`). Read `commits.walked: 0` with this in mind: 0 with true here is a warm store with nothing to do, and 0 with false is a repository with no history.

phases_ms.description: Where the run's wall clock went, in whole milliseconds, in run order (`reco-66q`). The keys are the phases of `fathom_analyze::index::run`, so a report that says "45 s" also says which 45 seconds they were.

store.description: Repository-relative path to the store this run wrote.

prune.description: What `--prune` removed (or, on `--dry-run`, would have): the commit rows no ref reaches, what cascaded with them, and what the review guard refused to touch. `null` when `--prune` was not passed — 'nothing was asked' is not the same statement as 'nothing was dead'.

commits_removed.description: `git_commit` rows removed: every one of them provably unreachable.

dry_run.description: True when `--dry-run` was passed. Every number below is then what a real prune *would* do, computed by the same statements rather than a second estimate.

episodes_removed.description: Episode rows that lost their last member to the prune and carried no decision, review or relink, so nothing pointed at them.

files_removed.description: `git_commit_file` rows that went with those commits.

refusal.description: Why the store deleted nothing because it could not tell dead rows from live ones — a break in the stored parent chain, or no ref tip to walk from. A refusal is a stated partial, not an error: the verb still exits 0.

sample.description: Up to twelve of the commit ids involved, newest first.

withheld_reviewed.description: Dead commits left in place because a review state or a mirrored ledger entry points at them (ADR-004 §8.2). Counted, never silently subtracted.

withheld_undecidable.description: Pairs with `refusal`: the rows that would have been candidates had the store been able to judge.

title: fathom index --json

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: OK
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the verb answered, and the index describes HEAD

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: ERROR
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: a rev that names nothing, an unimplemented verb, a rejected argument value

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: USAGE
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: clap rejected the command line (bad flag, unknown verb, missing value)

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: NOT_A_REPOSITORY
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: --root is not a git repository, or `.git` is unreadable

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: CONFIG_INVALID
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: `fathom.toml` failed the schema, or a value is the wrong type

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: CANCELLED
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: a cancel handle was pulled mid-run

x-fathom-exit-codes.name: FEATURE_ABSENT
x-fathom-exit-codes.when: the verb needs a feature this binary was not built with
